ee-0aRY.title: Sign: blue direction sign, white text and outline
ee-0aRY.summary: Blue direction signs with white text and a white outline. In Finland the arrow is part of the border. Latvia has a more stylised arrow.

differs.how: Arrow is built into the white border

ee-9WKW.title: Language: street is "tänav" (tn), road is "tee"
ee-9WKW.summary: Street signs end in tänav (often tn) or tee. Many urban streets have no suffix. Finnish -tie looks similar.

ee-Amwu.title: Sign: blue and white signpost wrappings
ee-Amwu.summary: Blue and white wrapping around signposts is very common. Finland and Sweden have them too.

ee-BgPO.title: Coverage: late-autumn Gen 4, dark moody sky
ee-BgPO.summary: On one small island, all coverage is Gen 4 in late autumn (fallen brown leaves) with dark clouds near sunset. If you see both, guess there. Near Tartu also has some autumn coverage.

ee-DexW.title: Sign: bus stop sign with 4 windows
ee-DexW.summary: The bus on the bus stop sign has four windows. Latvia has five, but Lithuania has the identical sign.

ee-KNav.title: Pole: trident top, 1 insulator up, 2 sideways
ee-KNav.summary: A fairly common pole top with one insulator on top and two on the sides, like a trident.

ee-KPZE.title: Pole: small metal cap on wooden poles
ee-KPZE.summary: Most wooden poles have a small metal cap on top, like in Nordic countries. Latvia sometimes has them too.

ee-Kvsf.title: Sign: pedestrian sign, 3 stripes, shoes and neck
ee-Kvsf.summary: Pedestrian sign with 3 stripes and a detailed figure with shoes and a separate head. Lithuania has 3 stripes too but a plainer figure.

differs.how: Also 3 stripes, but a less detailed figure

ee-N5Yh.title: Houses: wood and white brick, steep metal roofs
ee-N5Yh.summary: Wood and white brick, with steep corrugated metal roofs and sometimes painted stone walls. Wooden buildings exist in all Baltic countries but are most common here.

ee-N6Ec.title: Bollard: round baton shape
ee-N6Ec.summary: Round, baton-like bollard with a rectangular reflector on the front and two round ones on the back, white or orange. Latvian and Lithuanian bollards look different.

differs.how: Thin, slightly curved shape with numbers

ee-SRyp.title: Google car: Gen 3 with green tint ("green blur")
ee-SRyp.summary: Older Gen 3 coverage often has a slight green tint over part of the picture. Latvia and Lithuania rarely do, but it also appears in Sweden, often on one island.

ee-UV37.title: Pole: mixed types, round wooden most common
ee-UV37.summary: A mix of pole types, the least consistent of the three Baltic countries. Round wooden poles are most common, sometimes with diagonal supports.

ee-VLAz.title: House numbers: oval blue plates
ee-VLAz.summary: Oval blue house numbers are fairly common. Rare in the other Baltic countries, but also seen in Russia.

ee-XXzb.title: Language: Ä Ö Ü Õ, related to Finnish
ee-XXzb.summary: A Finnic language close to Finnish. Look for Ä, Ö, Ü and especially Õ. Latvian and Lithuanian are unrelated and look very different.

ee-YCqH.title: Marker: blue km post perpendicular to road
ee-YCqH.summary: All Baltic countries use the same blue kilometre marker. Here it sits perpendicular to the road with numbers on both sides.

differs.how: Marker is parallel to the road, one-sided number

ee-ZNTy.title: Pole: square concrete with diagonal supports
ee-ZNTy.summary: A fair number of square concrete poles, often with diagonal braces. Lithuania has similar ones.

ee-ZYAH.title: Guardrail: A-type with no reflectors
ee-ZYAH.summary: Normal A-type guardrails with no reflectors at all. The other two Baltic countries can have them.

ee-bdr3.title: Road lines: outer edge in short dashes
ee-bdr3.summary: Outer road lines sometimes made of short dashes. Lithuania sometimes has them, and Sweden mostly uses them.

ee-eXbS.title: Chevron: red with white arrows
ee-eXbS.summary: Red chevrons with white arrows. Russia and Ukraine use the same. Latvia and Lithuania use the opposite: white with red arrows.

ee-hkpv.title: Sign: thin red border, no white outline
ee-hkpv.summary: Warning and speed signs have a thin red border that runs right to the edge, with no white outline.

differs.how: Thick red border with thin white outline

ee-ki6y.title: Landscape: flat, hilly only in the south-east
ee-ki6y.summary: Mostly flat: just 10% of land is above 100 m and the highest point is 318 m. The hilliest parts are the south-east and the southern half of one northern county.

ee-lh3B.title: Sign: Russian Cyrillic next to local language
ee-lh3B.summary: In the north-east around the border town there is a large Russian minority, so some bilingual signs use Cyrillic. Most signs are still local, with Cyrillic occasionally elsewhere.

ee-lm-740900.title: Sign: black street sign, white frame
ee-lm-740900.summary: Street signs are black with white text inside a white frame, and dots in the corners. Seen in the second-largest city.

ee-nAUS.title: Houses: preserved medieval old town
ee-nAUS.summary: The capital old town is an almost perfectly preserved area of medieval and Renaissance buildings. In places it looks like central European cities.

ee-vr14.title: Plate: long white, blue EU strip on left
ee-vr14.summary: Long white plates with the standard blue European strip on the left.

ee-xf22.title: Google car: Gen 3 on very thin rural roads
ee-xf22.summary: Gen 3 coverage reaches many tiny rural roads here, more than in the other Baltics. Use it only as a last resort when guessing between them.
